Fwd: FYSA FOLLOW UP: META/FB Points of Contact and Trainings
Friday, September 23, 2022 at 6:41:55 PM Eastern Daylight
[contact omitted] Amanda Fagerblom
Time
To: [contact omitted] Philip Czajkowski
Cc: [contact omitted] Daniel Dedeyan, [contact omitted] Jannie Kwok
Hello Phil - Here's the write-up for potential platform engagement we talked about today. A lot of this is based on our
experience and that of our partners, as well as the regular threat assessment Meta shares regularly.
Happy to answer any questions you may have.
Allbest,
Amanda
Forwarded message ----
From: Amanda Fagerblom <[contact omitted]>
Date: Mon, 22 Aug 2022 at 11:35
Subject: Fwd: FYSA FOLLOW UP: META/FB Points of Contact and Trainings
To: Nora Pinzon <[contact omitted]>, Daniel Dedeyan <[contact omitted]>
CC: Cara Thanassi <[contact omitted]>, Carrie Mitchell <[contact omitted]>
Hello Nora and Danny - Following up on the USAID LAC conversation with Meta/FB, please see Cara's email below and
the attachment from Meta/FB. A phone call with Mission leadership, LAC bureau, and Meta/FB would be helpful given the
sensitivities and security concerns around programming in country. The notes below are for us/USAID (but comfortable
sharing to Meta/FB by phone)
I think continued engagement would be useful. Here is some initial thinking:
General points:
• Who is the Meta/FB POC for Nicaragua?
• What are the ongoing, FB-funded initiatives/support in Nicaragua (or regional that include Nicaragua)? I had
heard there was something around connectivity along the border with Honduras (regional) when I was with
Internews. This would be helpful to know so we can ensure our radio/media partners are aware of potential
• Stressing the point: the information space is radilly closing with very few on the ground professional reporters.
In-country media and digital literacy is incredibly low despite high mobile penetration rates, leaving many
Nicaraguans -in particular those new to the online world- susceptible to misinformation.
• Given the significant number of Nicaraguans forced into exile in Costa Rica, Mission stresses the importance
for Meta/FB to incorporate strategies for Costa Rica to include Nicaraguan diaspora.
• Costa Rica-Nicaragua Initiatives: Many of our Nicaraguan media, business, and civil society partners are
operating bi-nationally, legally registered in Costa Rica, but with main audiences and content in and related to
• Mission is looking at medium-term planning and worst-case scenarios that include internet disruptions and
blocking, coordinated account takedowns of independent media, small enterprises, and civil society social media
accounts, among others. The overarching concern for us is the timeline. Space is closing rapidly and
increasingly looking like a Cuba scenario.
Areas I see helpful collaboration for Nicaragua under Meta/FB lines of Central America support:
1. Elections and Integrity Efforts: Investigations and Account Removals. Despite the Municipal elections in
November 2022 being called already with opposition in jail and forced exile, we anticipate the regime to silence
independent voices in social media and carry out coordinated misinformation campaigns and coordinated
account takedown attacks via troll networks. Investigations into the coordination (potentially increased over
elections) may help us better understand the real risk and increased capacities of adversaries online so we can
better adapt our digital security training and online safety for Nicaraguan partners. The quarterly adversarial threat
report and coordinated inauthentic behavior report have been useful. With regard to the OAS cooperation
agreement Meta/FB signed with the OAS, we want to know how our partners can plug into that.
2. Circulating phishing campaigns targeting Nicaraguans in WhatsApp: Our Nicaraguan partners and digital
security trainers have noted an increase in instances of these campaigns in Nicaraguan WhatsApp groups. If your

task force working on this line has any one-pagers or visuals in Spanish to raise awareness and/or details for
reporting misuse we would very much welcome that to include in our training toolkits.
3. Trusted Partners Program: We would be interested in knowing what this includes. Many of our independent
media partners face coordinated social media account takedown attacks (ToS violations, etc.) and impersonated
fake accounts in their names. Does this program offer a rapid response to those crises?
4. We Think Digital/Meta Blueprint (digital/media literacy, online entrepreneurship for youth, and economic
growth online): Mission is looking at how to work with our Nicaraguan partners (youth entrepreneurship,
independent media, and other civil society organizations) to increase digital literacy and raise awareness about
misinformation among their audiences and beyond. As many Nicaraguan entities are forced into exile in Costa
Rica, they are looking to expand their economic growth online, so we would like to hear more about Meta/FB
Programs to Support Entrepreneurs and Small Business Owners (Nicaraguans in Nicaragua and Nicaraguans
in Costa Rica).
Happy to add or expand on any of these. This was what stood out to me.
Allbest,
Amanda
Amanda Fagerblom
Technical Officer
USAID I Nicaragua

<[contact omitted]>, Matthew Rees <[contact omitted]>, Michael Camilleri <[contact omitted]>, Ariana Scurti
<[contact omitted]>, Caitlyn Davis <[contact omitted]>, Michael Samras <[contact omitted]>, Russell Porter
<[contact omitted]>, Colleen Jones <[contact omitted]>
Hi All,
Thanks to those of you who participated in the call with META/FB on July 22. Attached, they have provided points of
contact for your respective countries, a description of their activities, and trainings that you, other mission staff, and,
potentially, IPs could benefit from. Given that there may be interest in training from multiple missions/posts, I'm happy to
serve as a focal point for coordinating that with META/FB so just reach out. Where you may want to flag issues of
country-level concern for META/FB POC, I would ask that you keep myself, the desks, and Michael on copy.
Pleaseshare this information with your teams and let us know if you have any follow up concerns or questions.
Best,
Cara

Michael,
Thank you again for the productive call we recently had with you and your team. We look forward
to continuing this conversation and our collaboration.
As discussed, please see attached the information requested during our briefing, including a
compilation of trainings as well as relevant points of contact for follow-up.
If you would like further details on any of these issues, please let us know.
Many thanks again for your partnership on these important issues.
Best,
Sandy
